items.question: A firm's costs are Rs 400 lakh: materials Rs 160 lakh, labour Rs 120 lakh, overheads Rs 80 lakh and transport Rs 40 lakh. Next year materials rise by 25%, labour falls by 10%, overheads stay the same and transport rises by 50%. Consider the following statements. (1) Materials will be the largest cost next year. (2) Labour plus transport next year will equal materials next year. (3) Total costs will rise by 12 percent next year. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Next year the costs are materials 160 x 1.25 = 200, labour 120 x 0.9 = 108, overheads 80 and transport 40 x 1.5 = 60, a total of 448 lakh. Materials at 200 is the largest cost. Labour plus transport is 168, not 200. Total costs rise by 48/400 = 12%. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

items.question: The repo rate rises from 6 percent to 6.5 percent. A firm has a borrowing of Rs 20 lakh charged at the repo rate. Consider the following statements. (1) The annual interest on the borrowing rises from Rs 1,20,000 to Rs 1,30,000. (2) The annual interest rises by Rs 10,000. (3) The rise in interest is more than 10 percent of the old interest. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 6 percent of 20 lakh is 1,20,000 and 6.5 percent of 20 lakh is 1,30,000. Statement 2 is correct: 1,30,000 minus 1,20,000 is 10,000. Statement 3 is incorrect: 10,000 out of 1,20,000 is about 8.3 percent, which is less than 10 percent.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Static GK

items.question: The dollar rate rises from Rs 80 to Rs 84. The euro rate rises from Rs 85 to Rs 88.40. Consider the following statements. (1) The rupee falls by 5 percent against the dollar. (2) The rupee falls by 4 percent against the euro. (3) The dollar rises by more in percentage terms than the euro. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 4 out of 80 is 5 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 3.40 out of 85 is 4 percent. Statement 3 is correct: 5 percent is more than 4 percent.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Static GK

items.question: Real gross domestic product adjusts nominal gross domestic product for changes in prices. Nominal gross domestic product is Rs 110 crore and the price index has risen by 10 percent from its base value of 100. Consider the following statements. (1) Real gross domestic product is Rs 100 crore. (2) Nominal gross domestic product overstates growth when prices rise. (3) Real gross domestic product is Rs 110 crore. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 110 divided by 1.10 is 100. Statement 2 is correct: the nominal figure includes the price rise, so it overstates the growth in actual output. Statement 3 is incorrect: 110 is the nominal figure, not the real one.

items.question: An airline's bookings fell from June, only on the route a rival began serving in June, while other routes were unchanged. Three explanations are offered: a fare rise in May that applied to all routes, fog cancellations in December, and the rival's new route in June. Consider the following statements. (1) The fare rise is ruled out, because it applied to all routes but the fall is only on one route. (2) The fog cancellations are ruled out, because they happened in December while the fall began in June. (3) The rival's new route is supported as a cause, because the fall matches it in place and in timing. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: a change affecting all routes cannot explain a fall on one route only. Statement 2 is correct: a December event cannot cause a fall that began in June. Statement 3 is correct: the fall is confined to the rival's route and began when the rival began serving it.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Static GK

items.question: A central bank targets inflation of 4 percent, with a tolerance band from 2 percent to 6 percent. Inflation is 1.5 percent. Consider the following statements. (1) Inflation is below the target. (2) Inflation is within the tolerance band. (3) Inflation has breached the tolerance band. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 1.5 is less than 4. Statement 2 is incorrect: 1.5 is below the bottom of the band at 2. Statement 3 is correct: 1.5 is below 2, so the band is breached.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Static GK

items.question: A country's services exports were Rs 200 crore in 2021, Rs 260 crore in 2022, Rs 312 crore in 2023 and Rs 374.4 crore in 2024. Consider the following statements. (1) The fastest growth was in 2022. (2) Total growth from 2021 to 2024 was 87.2 percent. (3) Services exports nearly doubled from 2021 to 2024. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: growth was 30 percent in 2022, 20 percent in 2023 and 20 percent in 2024, so 2022 was the fastest. Statement 2 is correct: 374.4 minus 200 is 174.4, and 174.4 out of 200 is 87.2 percent. Statement 3 is incorrect: doubling would need 400, and 374.4 is less than 400.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Financial Concepts

items.question: Five mutual funds have assets under management of Rs 400 crore, Rs 320 crore, Rs 240 crore, Rs 160 crore and Rs 80 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) The fund with Rs 320 crore is second in the ranking. (2) The largest fund is five times the smallest fund. (3) The funds with Rs 240 crore and Rs 160 crore together exceed the largest fund. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 320 is the second largest of the five figures. Statement 2 is correct: 400 is five times 80. Statement 3 is incorrect: 240 plus 160 is 400, which equals the largest fund, so it does not exceed it.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Current Affairs

items.question: The Narasimham Committee on banking reforms was set up in 1991. The Chelliah Committee on tax reforms was set up in 1991. The Tarapore Committee on capital account convertibility was set up in 1997. Consider the following statements. (1) The Narasimham Committee and the Chelliah Committee were set up in the same year. (2) The Tarapore Committee came later than the other two. (3) The gap between the Narasimham Committee and the Tarapore Committee is 6 years. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: both were set up in 1991. Statement 2 is correct: 1997 comes after 1991. Statement 3 is correct: 1997 minus 1991 is 6.

items.question: A trade bloc has 10 members: 6 from Asia and 4 from elsewhere. Consider the following statements. (1) Asian members are 60 percent of the bloc. (2) Non-Asian members are fewer than half of the bloc. (3) Asian members are double the non-Asian members. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 6 out of 10 is 60 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 4 out of 10 is 40 percent, which is fewer than half. Statement 3 is incorrect: double 4 is 8, not 6.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Financial Concepts

items.question: A country's budget is Rs 4,500 crore: defence Rs 900 crore, education Rs 675 crore, health Rs 450 crore and other items Rs 2,475 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) Defence accounts for 20 percent of the budget. (2) Education accounts for 15 percent of the budget. (3) Health accounts for one-tenth of the budget. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 900 out of 4,500 is 20 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 675 out of 4,500 is 15 percent. Statement 3 is correct: 450 out of 4,500 is one-tenth.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Financial Concepts

items.question: The cash reserve ratio falls from 4.5 percent to 4.0 percent. A bank has deposits of Rs 2,000 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) The reserve the bank must keep falls from Rs 90 crore to Rs 80 crore. (2) Rs 10 crore of the bank's money is freed. (3) The freed amount is one-ninth of the old reserve. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 4.5 percent of 2,000 is 90 and 4 percent of 2,000 is 80. Statement 2 is correct: 90 minus 80 is 10. Statement 3 is correct: 10 out of 90 is one-ninth.
items.topic: Economic and Business Environment - Financial Concepts

items.question: Fund A gives a return of 10 percent on an investment of Rs 2 lakh. Fund B gives a return of 12 percent on an investment of Rs 1.5 lakh. Consider the following statements. (1) Fund A's gain is larger in rupees than fund B's. (2) Fund B's rate of return is higher than fund A's. (3) Fund B's gain is larger in rupees than fund A's. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: A gains 10 percent of 2 lakh, or Rs 20,000, while B gains 12 percent of 1.5 lakh, or Rs 18,000. Statement 2 is correct: 12 percent is higher than 10 percent. Statement 3 is incorrect: B's Rs 18,000 is less than A's Rs 20,000.

items.question: Foreign direct investment involves a lasting business presence in the country. Portfolio investment does not involve a lasting business presence. A foreign bank opens a branch in India with an investment of Rs 1,000 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) The branch is foreign direct investment. (2) The branch is a portfolio investment. (3) The branch involves a lasting business presence. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: opening a branch is a lasting business presence with a large investment, which is foreign direct investment. Statement 2 is incorrect: portfolio investment is buying stocks and bonds, not opening a branch. Statement 3 is correct: a branch is a lasting presence by definition.

items.question: Gold prices rose by 8 percent in a month. Three explanations are offered: a fall in the rupee this month, higher festival demand this month, and a new mine discovery last year. Further facts: the rupee fell by 6 percent this month, festival demand rose in the same month, and the mine discovery was a year ago. Consider the following statements. (1) The mine discovery is ruled out by timing, because it happened a year ago. (2) The fall in the rupee is supported as a cause, because a weaker rupee raises the rupee price of gold. (3) Festival demand is ruled out as a cause. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: a discovery a year ago cannot explain a rise this month. Statement 2 is correct: gold is priced in dollars, so a weaker rupee raises its rupee price in the same month. Statement 3 is incorrect: festival demand rose in the same month as the price rise, so it is not ruled out.

items.question: A bank must keep its net non-performing asset ratio below 6 percent. Its net non-performing assets are Rs 30 crore and its net advances are Rs 600 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) The bank's net non-performing asset ratio is 5 percent. (2) The bank is within the limit. (3) The ratio would breach the limit if net advances fell to Rs 400 crore. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 30 out of 600 is 5 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 5 is less than 6. Statement 3 is correct: 30 out of 400 is 7.5 percent, which is above 6.

items.question: Credit card spending was Rs 100 crore in 2021, Rs 130 crore in 2022, Rs 156 crore in 2023 and Rs 187.2 crore in 2024. Consider the following statements. (1) The fastest growth was in 2022. (2) Total growth from 2021 to 2024 was 87.2 percent. (3) Spending in 2024 was more than 1.8 times spending in 2021. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

items.question: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award. The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award. Both awards were instituted in 1954. The Padma Shri is the third-highest civilian award, also instituted in 1954. Consider the following statements. (1) The Bharat Ratna ranks above the Padma Vibhushan. (2) The Padma Shri ranks above the Padma Vibhushan. (3) A gallery that places the Padma Vibhushan above the Bharat Ratna has the two awards in the wrong order. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: The Bharat Ratna ranks above the Padma Vibhushan, so the first statement is correct and a gallery placing the Vibhushan above the Ratna has them in the wrong order. The Padma Shri is the third-highest award, so it ranks below, not above, the Padma Vibhushan, and the second statement is false.
